reviewScope: All 29 pinned lab bodies retrieved during source review; topic-level adaptations and selected technical guidance corrections. Some long bodies were condensed for review. Not a claim of per-operation, media or every link validation. Local practice uses fictional data.

rows.title: Lab 00: Safe tenant and subscription preflight
rows.reason: Replace mandatory trial signup with authorization and existing entitlement checks.
rows.prereq: Approved tenant, named admin, scoped access; no trials or purchases.
rows.mechanism: Tenant is a directory; subscription is a resource/billing boundary; license enables feature. Verify tenant ID, role, entitlement and resource scope before any operation.
rows.practice: Entra Free tenant, no subscription: classify directory read, CA, PIM, VM deployment.
rows.answer: Authorized read may be possible. CA and PIM require applicable existing licenses; VM deployment needs authorized subscription and budget. Use local alternatives.

rows.title: Lab 01: Provision, delegate, recover and license users
rows.reason: Retain individual, CSV and Graph provisioning; reject shared passwords, ForceChangePasswordNextSignIn=false, plain-text credential storage and dated installer.
rows.prereq: User Administrator for eligible user creation, Privileged Role Administrator for role assignment, License Administrator and available seats.
rows.mechanism: UPN identifies sign-in; object ID identifies object; roles grant privileges, licenses enable services. App registration defaults differ from enterprise app management. Soft-deleted user normally recoverable 30 days.
rows.practice: Model Chris: create unique temporary credential with forced change, reject duplicate CSV UPN, add/remove Application Administrator, delete/restore and assign existing seat.
rows.answer: Check new-session permissions before/after role change; verify restored object and dependent assignments independently. No purchase on seat exhaustion. Graph permissions and directory role are both evaluated.

rows.title: Lab 02: Tenant properties, domains and privacy
rows.reason: Separate verified custom domains from onmicrosoft.com management; reject assumed fabricated subdomain and using sample privacy PDF as legal policy.
rows.prereq: Authorized domain/property administrator, approved DNS ownership proof and legal notice.
rows.mechanism: Tenant ID stays stable on display rename. Domain proof validates namespace; UPN and region are separate. Privacy contact/URL publishes notice, not authorization.
rows.practice: Classify display rename, custom domain verification, onmicrosoft.com fallback domain, technical contact and privacy statement.
rows.answer: Verify DNS proof only for authorized domain; use supported Microsoft 365 fallback-domain flow. Check notice from user view; no actual DNS or production changes.

rows.title: Lab 03: Group membership and licensing
rows.reason: Retain security/M365 groups, assigned/dynamic membership, licensing; reject broad all-user rules without impact review.
rows.prereq: Groups Administrator, License Administrator, eligible existing licenses, seats and usage location.
rows.mechanism: Dynamic rules evaluate attributes asynchronously. Group license is inherited; direct assignment can coexist. M365 groups support collaboration.
rows.practice: Sales member, Finance member, Sales guest; rule Sales AND Member; one directly licensed user and insufficient seats. Predict assignment and removal.
rows.answer: Only Sales member matches. Capacity, conflicting service plans or location can block assignment. Direct license can survive group removal. Check per-user license errors in M365 admin center.

rows.title: Lab 04: External collaboration policy boundaries
rows.reason: Keep guest visibility, invite roles, domain allow/deny and OTP. Do not enable self-service indiscriminately or call OTP universally strongest.
rows.prereq: Authorized external identities admin, approved domains and test identities.
rows.mechanism: Guest directory visibility, invitation authorization, domain restriction, cross-tenant access and resource grants are distinct.
rows.practice: Compare allowed partner and denied unknown domain; existing redeemed guest; authorized inviter vs guest; existing SharePoint grant.
rows.answer: New invitation may be blocked independently of resource access. Domain restriction is not retroactive blanket revocation of redeemed access; check resource sharing and existing assignments.

rows.title: Lab 05: Invite, redeem and verify B2B identity
rows.reason: Retain CSV and Graph invitation; replace broad User.ReadWrite.All with least-privileged User.Invite.All where applicable. No real invitations.
rows.prereq: Guest Inviter or authorized role per policy; validated email and redirect; approved Graph scope.
rows.mechanism: Invitation creates/uses guest object; sendInvitationMessage controls mail; redemption state and resource grant are separate.
rows.practice: Model valid address, missing redirect and duplicate; draft fictional invitation with sendInvitationMessage false; compare pending, accepted, resource-assigned.
rows.answer: Reject invalid input; inspect existing object. Verify guest ID, redemption and resource grant independently. Do not contact actual addresses.

rows.title: Lab 06: Google federation and external trust
rows.reason: Retain OAuth client, redirects, test audience and redemption. Reject shared Google accounts, plain-text secrets, universal Bluetooth/passkey claim.
rows.prereq: Approved existing provider project/workforce tenant, authorized test identity and secure secret store.
rows.mechanism: IdP authenticates guest; Entra binds identity and issues resource token. Client ID is identifier, secret confidential; callback exact match matters.
rows.practice: Model correct callback, wrong callback, expired secret and successful sign-in without app grant.
rows.answer: Wrong callback/expired secret fail federation; successful authentication is not authorization. Verify issuer, redirect, redemption and app grant. No external project created.

rows.title: Lab 07: Hybrid sync without provisioning
rows.reason: Keep AD infrastructure, UPN, Connect installation, inbound rules, staged sync, PTA and hybrid join. Reject old VM template/trial provisioning and insecure credentials; detailed commands not fully qualified.
rows.prereq: Approved existing supported AD/Connect environment, Hybrid Identity Administrator and on-prem rights. No VM or trial.
rows.mechanism: Import, join/transform, export; verified UPN controls sign-in suffix, source anchor links identities. Scope changes can delete objects; staging previews exports. PHS/PTA/federation are distinct.
rows.practice: Model three users/two suffixes; include approved suffix, exclude remainder; inspect staged adds/deletes; compare PHS/PTA outage; interpret DomainJoined YES/AzureAdJoined NO.
rows.answer: Abort unexpected deletion and preserve deletion guard. PTA requires agents; PHS uses synced hash in cloud. Hybrid join requires both domain and Entra state. No real exports.

rows.title: Lab 08: Modern MFA methods and enforcement
rows.reason: Supersede legacy MFA method management retired September 30, 2025; per-user MFA is legacy enforcement; no shared admin passwords or app-password rollout.
rows.prereq: Authentication Policy Administrator; CA Administrator and existing P1 for CA. Free security defaults are separate.
rows.mechanism: Methods policy permits methods, registration binds credentials, CA requires factor/strength during sign-in. Registered does not mean every session challenged.
rows.practice: Fictional Delia registered push and passkey; pilot policy requires phishing-resistant strength; compare passkey, password+push, out-of-scope and report-only.
rows.answer: Supported passkey may satisfy strength; push alone does not satisfy phishing-resistant strength. Report-only logs projected effect. Verify sign-in policy and auth details.

rows.title: Lab 09: SSPR and combined registration
rows.reason: Retain pilot, scope, registration and positive/negative tests; use unified methods policy instead of legacy method toggles.
rows.prereq: Authorized SSPR admin and applicable existing license; hybrid writeback prerequisites separate.
rows.mechanism: Scope determines eligibility, methods policy defines proof, registration records methods. Cloud reset and AD writeback are separate.
rows.practice: Allan pilot member with two proofs, Grady outside pilot, synced user without writeback; predict reset outcomes.
rows.answer: Allan succeeds only with required proofs, Grady not in scope, hybrid reset needs writeback when applicable. Verify audit and fresh sign-in without touching real users.

rows.title: Lab 10: Entra VM login without weakening RDP
rows.reason: Keep managed identity, Windows/Linux extensions and VM login RBAC; reject default disabling NLA/CredSSP.
rows.prereq: Existing approved VM, supported OS/client, identity, extension, RBAC and network; no new compute.
rows.mechanism: VM User Login vs Administrator Login governs OS access; Contributor alone does not grant OS login. Windows RDP and Linux SSH have distinct flows.
rows.practice: Reader, Contributor, VM User Login: predict OS vs management access; troubleshoot missing extension, wrong tenant, network.
rows.answer: VM User Login is separate non-admin permission; verify extension, scope, client and network. Use supported web-account RDP or OpenSSH; no insecure port/security changes.

rows.title: Lab 11: Eligible Azure resource role
rows.reason: Keep PIM eligibility, activation, duration and removal; source explicitly blocks some actual tasks. Global Admin alone is not Azure resource authority.
rows.prereq: Existing P2/Governance and authorized resource-scope role-assignment administrator.
rows.mechanism: Azure RBAC scope is independent of directory role. Eligible is not active; activation follows configured approval/MFA and time.
rows.practice: Engineer eligible API Management Contributor on one resource group, approval required, 1h. Compare pending, approved, expired, unrelated scope.
rows.answer: Only active approved window grants scoped role. Verify schedule/request and active assignment, expiration, negative test. No live elevation.

rows.title: Lab 12: Smart lockout versus password protection
rows.reason: Separate cloud lockout duration/threshold from on-prem banned-password audit/enforce mode. Never lock real accounts for a lab.
rows.prereq: Existing P1+ for customization, approved auth policy admin.
rows.mechanism: Smart lockout considers familiar/unfamiliar behavior and avoids counting repeated identical bad hashes; AD lockout is distinct.
rows.practice: Synthetic repeated identical and distinct failures; compare cloud and AD threshold with PTA; identify evidence.
rows.answer: Raw event count alone is insufficient. Coordinate cloud/AD controls and inspect sign-in evidence; simulate lockout only.

rows.title: Lab 13: Policy impact before enforcement
rows.reason: Source text reviewed in full. Accept scoped user/resource assignment, policy evaluation, testing, rollback and session-control concepts. Supersede blanket Global Administrator assumption and immediate enforcement; do not disable Security Defaults solely for practice. Azure Monitor workbook can have separate costs; don't enable it.
rows.prereq: Authorized isolated tenant with applicable Conditional Access license (typically P1 for included users), Conditional Access Administrator or approved equivalent, approved test identity/resource, emergency access and rollback plan. Local model needs none.
rows.mechanism: Assignments decide whether a policy is in scope. The grant control determines whether access is blocked or allowed subject to requirements; session controls constrain an already-authorized session. Report-only computes impact and logs results without enforcing the policy. What If is a modeled evaluation of specified inputs, not proof that every runtime dependency or sign-in is covered.
rows.practice: In the local model create a fictional report-only policy targeting Debra and Sway with Block access. Compare Debra/Sway, Debra/another app, and a second user/Sway. Predict whether policy applies and whether access is actually blocked. Switch the fictional state to On and repeat, then return it to Off. Model sign-in frequency as a separate session policy rather than as an immediate account block.
rows.answer: Debra/Sway is in scope. Report-only records the would-block result without enforcing it; other combinations are not in scope. On enforces the block for a matching request. Off does not evaluate the policy. Verify in actual approved sign-in logs where available; an existing session, cached token, policy propagation and other policies can affect runtime observations. Never change real Security Defaults or enable a policy just to pass this course.

rows.title: Lab 14: Risk-based Conditional Access
rows.reason: Keep separate user/sign-in risks and remediation; replace immediate all-user enforcement with pilot/report-only review.
rows.prereq: Existing P2/eligible suite, CA admin, approved scope and usable strong credentials.
rows.mechanism: User risk estimates account compromise; sign-in risk estimates illegitimate request. Detection, policy and remediation differ.
rows.practice: A high user risk/low sign-in, B reverse, C neither. Model high-risk report-only and hypothetical enforcement.
rows.answer: A user-risk policy, B sign-in-risk policy, C neither. Report-only not enforcement; confirm current compatible grants, emergency access and audit.

rows.title: Lab 15: MFA registration policy and adoption
rows.reason: Distinguish licensed ID Protection registration policy, registration campaign and CA Register security information user action.
rows.prereq: Existing P2 for ID Protection registration policy, authorized method admin, licensed CA when relevant.
rows.mechanism: Registration enables proof; campaign nudges; registration CA secures enrollment; sign-in CA controls access.
rows.practice: Not registered, SMS registered, passkey registered: compare adoption and phishing-resistant sign-in requirement.
rows.answer: Registration status does not prove strength or actual MFA usage. Verify registration and sign-in evidence separately.

rows.title: Lab 16: Managed identity and Key Vault authorization
rows.reason: Prefer RBAC over broad Secret Management access policy; do not print secrets/tokens or assume archival API version current.
rows.prereq: Approved existing VM/vault, managed identity, network and data-plane RBAC; no new Azure resource.
rows.mechanism: System-assigned identity lifecycle tied to resource. Correct audience plus resource role required; Key Vault Contributor does not grant secret read.
rows.practice: Compare Graph audience vs vault audience, Key Vault Reader vs Secrets User, unrelated scope.
rows.answer: Wrong audience fails; correct audience without permission denied; approved Secrets User can read within scope. Check networking and role propagation; never expose real secret.

rows.title: Lab 17: Discovery versus app enforcement
rows.reason: Sanction/unsanction label alone is not universal blocking; requires configured supported endpoint integration or other control.
rows.prereq: Existing Defender for Cloud Apps and supported Endpoint integration, authorized security role.
rows.mechanism: Discovery observes telemetry, catalog risk describes app, sanction status expresses policy; enforcement depends on managed device and control.
rows.practice: Managed/unmanaged devices access fictional app; compare tag only and integrated enforcement.
rows.answer: Tag is not proof of block. Verify endpoint policy and logs, supported device and exception. No real restriction.

rows.title: Lab 18: Conditional Access App Control
rows.reason: Separate CA report-only from Defender monitor-only; app and client support matter. No live alert email.
rows.prereq: Existing CA P1 and Defender for Cloud Apps, supported application and approved admin.
rows.mechanism: CA authorizes and routes supported sessions; Defender policy monitors or enforces based on filters. Banner alone is not data protection proof.
rows.practice: Pradeep uses Forms from compliant/unmanaged device; compare outside scope, report-only, enabled monitor-only.
rows.answer: Only applicable supported routed sessions get control; monitor observes not blocks. Verify sign-in and activity logs; native clients may differ.

rows.title: Lab 19: App registration, scopes and app roles
rows.reason: Correct delegated scope versus application role; never store real secret in Notepad; custom credential permissions do not automatically grant app assignments.
rows.prereq: Approved app owner/administrator; applicable custom-role entitlement and Privileged Role Admin when required.
rows.mechanism: Application is definition, service principal tenant instance; public SPA uses PKCE no secret; confidential client approved credential. API validates issuer/audience/expiry plus scp or roles.
rows.practice: Employees API: delegated read, app-only read role, wrong audience, delegated write but user read-only. Map redirect and custom role permissions.
rows.answer: Correct flow plus resource permission required. Wrong audience fails; delegated scope cannot override user authority. Distinguish app roles and custom directory roles.

rows.title: Lab 20: Enterprise app assignment versus enforcement
rows.reason: Assignment alone does not always restrict all users; Assignment required setting and downstream app authorization matter.
rows.prereq: Approved existing app, app administrator or owner; appropriate group assignment entitlement. No SaaS signup.
rows.mechanism: Service principal holds assignments and settings; SSO authenticates, SCIM provisions, app RBAC authorizes.
rows.practice: Adele assigned, Alex not; compare Assignment required Yes/No, disabled app and missing downstream account.
rows.answer: Yes restricts unassigned ordinary users under supported flow; No may permit sign-in subject to other rules. Verify Entra and app-side authorization separately.

rows.title: Lab 21: Consent is a permission grant, not app registration
rows.reason: Full source text reviewed. Preserve configured-permission review, app registration versus enterprise application distinction, and tenant-wide grant caution. Correct blanket Global Administrator requirement: role capability depends on requested permission type; Privileged Role Administrator can grant consent for Microsoft Graph application permissions, whereas Cloud Application Administrator and Application Administrator cannot grant Graph app roles. Do not mechanically regrant existing consent.
rows.prereq: Fictional app and resource service principal for local exercise. Real consent requires approved app, publisher and scope verification, correct role, change authorization, and review of existing grants. No actual consent executed.
rows.mechanism: An application registration describes requested permissions; the enterprise app represents the service principal in a tenant. Delegated grants authorize access on behalf of a signed-in user, subject to user authorization. Application grants give the service principal access without a user and are represented by app role assignments. Listing a permission on an app registration is not proof of effective consent.
rows.practice: Fictional Demo App requests delegated User.Read and application Directory.ReadWrite.All. A Cloud Application Administrator is asked to approve both. Decide which grant is supportable by the role and whether either is justified by a read-only profile feature. Record client ID, resource API, requested permission type, approved grant, reviewer and before/after evidence; explain rollback.
rows.answer: User.Read delegated may be permitted by the applicable consent policy and administrator authority. The Graph application role cannot be granted by that administrator; a more privileged authorized role would be required, and the broad write request is unjustified for this feature. Reject it, inspect existing delegated grants and app role assignments separately, and verify a least-privilege token and denied write. No actual token or tenant-wide grant is needed.

rows.title: Lab 22: Catalog ownership, resources and guest review
rows.reason: Full source text reviewed. The prerequisite paragraph describes Terms of Use rather than catalog management and recommends a trial; supersede it with feature-specific governance licensing and catalog delegation guidance. The source mixes an enabled catalog with an optional staging state, and combines guest access review with catalog administration; teach those as separate operations.
rows.prereq: Existing eligible governance entitlement for the precise feature; authorized Identity Governance Administrator or delegated catalog creator/owner with resource-specific rights as applicable. Approved existing test resources only. No trial, paid subscription, real guest removal or production changes.
rows.mechanism: A catalog organizes governed resources and access packages. Adding a group, app or site to a catalog makes it available for package design, not an immediate grant to a requester. Catalog owners manage their catalog; package policy defines who can request, approval and duration. A separate review evaluates existing access. A catalog cannot be deleted while it contains access packages.
rows.practice: In a fictional Marketing catalog add Retail Readers group and a demo enterprise app; make Adele a catalog owner but not tenant admin. Design an access package with manager approval and 30-day expiry. Explain what changes after adding the resource versus approval versus expiry. Stage a guest review separately and compare automatic removal with manual result review. Predict what happens when a catalog with a package is deleted.
rows.answer: Adding a resource changes catalog availability only; the approved package assignment grants the selected resource roles, and expiry ends package-governed access. Other independent grants may remain. A catalog-scoped role is not tenant administration. Delete or retire dependent packages through approved process before removing the catalog. Validate review target, reviewer availability and nonresponse policy before any real auto-apply.

rows.title: Lab 23: Terms of use and consent evidence
rows.reason: Keep PDF/version, expiry, CA grant, report and editing. Per-device acceptance is not universally appropriate; no shared admin password.
rows.prereq: Approved legal document, existing applicable CA license, authorized admin and pilot.
rows.mechanism: Terms object contains version and acceptance; CA requires acceptance; calendar expiry differs from individual duration. OAuth consent is separate.
rows.practice: Alice accepts Jan 1, Bob Jan 15; monthly calendar expiry vs 30-day duration; version 2 requiring reacceptance and decline.
rows.answer: Calendar next expiry Feb 1 for both in model; per-user duration differs. Decline blocks if required, excluded not targeted. Verify version and record; no actual enforcement.

rows.title: Lab 24: Governed guest lifecycle
rows.reason: Update narrow claim: guests invited through entitlement management or converted to governed can be lifecycle managed; independently granted resources may be affected.
rows.prereq: Existing entitlement management and authorized governance administrator; dependency inventory and recovery plan.
rows.mechanism: Final package expiry removes package access; governed guest lifecycle may block and delete account; unmanaged guests are separate.
rows.practice: A invited through package with extra SharePoint grant, B preexisting unmanaged, C converted governed; final package expires.
rows.answer: A/C may be blocked/deleted according to settings; B not automatically removed. Independent grants may remain until account action. Verify scope, history and dependencies before approved cleanup.

rows.title: Lab 25: Review group access versus privileged roles
rows.reason: Full source text reviewed. The scenario discusses privileged assignments, but its actual operation reviews membership of a Sales and Marketing group; do not treat group membership review as a PIM role review. Replace blanket Global Administrator assumption with scope-specific review roles; reviewer decisions and application of results are separate.
rows.prereq: Local fictional review: no license. Real group/app review requires applicable governance license (for basic scenarios Entra ID P2 or ID Governance as specified), suitable authorized role, valid target and reviewers, and approved removal policy.
rows.mechanism: Define target resource, population, reviewers, schedule, nonresponse behavior and how results are applied. A reviewer can approve or deny existing access. Denial is a decision until results are applied or automatic application is configured. A review of group membership is not automatically a review of Entra or Azure privileged role assignments; use PIM review for that distinct resource type.
rows.practice: Review three fictional Sales members: Alex approves one member, denies a transferred member and leaves a third unanswered. Predict outcome under manual application and under an approved auto-apply policy that removes nonresponses. Identify which audit evidence proves the decision and which proves membership actually changed. Now decide how to review an eligible Entra privileged role.
rows.answer: With manual application, a decision does not itself establish removal; review and apply approved results, then inspect membership. Auto-apply may remove denied and nonresponding members depending on configured settings. For eligible privileged role access use the appropriate PIM access review, not an unrelated group review. Keep records of reviewer, decision, applied results and post-review membership or role assignment.

rows.title: Lab 26: PIM approval, activation and limited scope
rows.reason: Keep eligibility, settings, approval, duration and removal; avoid shared passwords and single classroom admin as approver; source scope demo is not actual AU assignment.
rows.prereq: Existing P2/Governance, Privileged Role Administrator, approved independent approver and test identity.
rows.mechanism: Eligibility allows request; approval/activation creates time-limited privilege. AU scope limits supported operations; directory scope broader.
rows.practice: Miriam eligible Compliance Admin 2h: pending, denied, approved, expired; compare Sales AU User Admin with tenant-wide.
rows.answer: Pending/denied no privilege; approved time window only. Verify PIM history and scope; unrelated operation denied. No live role activation.

rows.title: Lab 27: Sentinel connectors and KQL without costs
rows.reason: Source optional lab unavailable; reject personal subscription/trial. Current Defender portal transition; use synthetic telemetry.
rows.prereq: Existing approved workspace/connector/permissions and explicit ingestion budget only for real work; no resources enabled.
rows.mechanism: Diagnostics route selected events; connectors do not prove completeness. SigninLogs and AuditLogs distinct. KQL filter/project and correlate.
rows.practice: Synthetic sign-ins with nonzero ResultType; audit role change. Query 24h, failures, project user/time/result; correlate by identity/time.
rows.answer: Empty results may mean no match, wrong range, latency or missing ingestion. Audit change not proof of attack. Use local synthetic tables.

rows.title: Lab 28: Identity Secure Score and risk remediation
rows.reason: Correct source summary: user risk, not sign-in risk. Example score and update time not universal; score is not proof of security.
rows.prereq: Authorized read role, existing P2 for real risk policy; CA admin and approval; local only.
rows.mechanism: Secure Score measures recommended controls. Recommendation, configured policy, effective behavior and score are separate.
rows.practice: 33 fictional unprotected users; draft report-only user risk policy with emergency access, registration and license checks.
rows.answer: Verify scope and policy state, report-only logs and gaps; score may lag. High score not proof of no compromise. No real change.
